abstract: In this paper we describe the first fully real-time indexing solution for pattern matching over an arbitrary integer alphabet. Our data structure spends $O(1)$ worst-case time w.h.p. for processing each new letter appended to $T$ and worst-case $O(|P|+occ)$ time for reporting all occurrences of $P$, where $T$ and $P$ are strings over an integer alphabet. The main idea of our solution is a novel representation of the suffix tree, the path-decomposed suffix tree, which does not store the full topology of the suffix tree but instead decomposes it into paths, each stored in a dictionary that encodes parent--child relationships indirectly.
hook: A string index now takes constant time per appended letter and optimal time per query.
summary: The authors give the first fully real-time index for pattern matching over integer alphabets, with O(1) worst-case time (with high probability) per appended letter and O(|P|+occ) per query. It rests on a path-decomposed suffix tree that stores paths in a dictionary instead of the full tree. It is a theoretical result, so practical speed is untested.
title: Real-Time String Indexing in Optimal Time
